title: Ines and the Letters
premise: Orsen Hartwell has spent seven years studying sea turtles on a remote coast, convinced that love, like migration, is something best observed from a safe distance. When her estranged aunt dies and leaves the family orchard jointly to Orsen and Ines Vale—the childhood friend she abandoned without explanation—the two are forced to share a house, a harvest, and the truth of why Orsen vanished. As the orchard's last viable season ticks toward a developer's deadline, Orsen learns that a heart, like a tide, cannot be contained forever. She chooses to stay, sign the deed whole, and build a family with Ines rather than flee into the sea again.
about_author: H. M. Brightwater is a former tide-pool docent who writes love stories set where land meets water. She lives in a converted cannery with two opinionated gulls and a shelf of unsent letters.

chapters.title: The Muscle That Lies
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Counting nesting turtles on a moonlit beach, Orsen rehearses her philosophy: the heart is trainable, containable. A lawyer's letter about an inheritance she never wanted arrives with the dawn tide. Emotional beat: armored solitude, faintly cracked by curiosity.

chapters.title: Two Names on One Deed
chapters.summary: Orsen arrives at Hartwell Orchard and discovers the deed names her and Ines Vale jointly—her childhood best friend, the person she left behind without a word. Ines is already there, furious, holding pruning shears like a verdict. Emotional beat: collision, guilt, unwilling attraction to the past.

chapters.title: What the Trees Remember
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines catalogs the orchard's dying trees and her own grievances while Orsen clumsily helps. A shared memory surfaces in the old letters hidden in the farmhouse wall—letters Ines wrote and never sent. Emotional beat: resentment loosening into wary tenderness.

chapters.title: Salt and Sap
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The developer's offer arrives: ninety days to buy out the other half or sell. Orsen proposes they co-run one harvest season to raise money. Working side by side, she notices Ines laughing again and hates how much she wants to be the cause. Emotional beat: hope she refuses to name.

chapters.title: The Festival of Borrowed Light
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The town's lantern festival pulls them both in; neighbors treat Orsen as family returned, not stranger. A near-kiss under paper lights is interrupted by news: the developer has raised the offer and the town is splitting. Emotional beat: belonging glimpsed, then threatened.

chapters.title: Letters Never Sent
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen reads the wall letters and learns Ines loved her for years before she fled—and that Orsen's mother hid Ines's replies, engineering the estrangement. Shaken, Orsen almost confesses, then retreats to the coast to count turtles again. Emotional beat: shame, the old escape reflex firing.

chapters.title: The Empty Nest Count
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines follows Orsen to the beach, finds her hollowed out by the truth, and instead of comfort demands honesty: 'You don't get to disappear twice.' They fight in the surf, say the unsayable, and part unresolved. Emotional beat: raw confrontation, love admitted in anger.

chapters.title: Ninety Days, Minus One
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Deadline looming, the town rallies a harvest festival to fund the buyout, but a storm flattens half the crop overnight. Orsen must choose between a research post abroad—her old safe harbor—and staying. Emotional beat: despair sharpening into decision.

chapters.title: The Whole Heart
chapters.summary: Climax. Orsen's POV. At the signing, the developer waits; Ines expects her to bolt. Orsen instead tears up the acceptance letter in front of the town, signs the deed in full, and tells Ines she's done lending pieces—she's risking the whole heart. Emotional beat: public vulnerability, the leap.

chapters.title: Where the Tide Comes In
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. One year later: the orchard saved, grafted with salt-hardy stock, the farmhouse wall letters framed. Ines writes one final letter and hands it to Orsen unsealed—a first, sent. They plant a tree together as the turtles come ashore. Emotional beat: belonging, chosen and kept.
